title: 2nd Mystery The Ease Of Essential Power

questions.question: What main idea is taught about Allah’s power in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s power can do countless things with the same ease as doing one thing.

questions.question: What are all created things compared to when speaking about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: They are compared to bright mirrors.

questions.question: Which kinds of things are said to obey Allah’s command, from the smallest to the largest?
questions.answer: Everything does, from tiny particles and living things to stars, suns, and moons.

questions.question: Why does one task not stop another task for Allah?
questions.answer: Because His power is unlimited, and nothing is hard for Him.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about big and small things for Allah’s power?
questions.answer: There is no difference between them for Allah’s power.

questions.question: What example shows that something very large can be moved in an easy, controlled way?
questions.answer: A huge ship can be moved as easily as a child moves a toy.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the commander who sends one soldier or a whole army with one order?
questions.answer: One command can direct both a single person and a large group.

questions.question: In the balance example, what happens when a small item is added?
questions.answer: It can make one side rise and the other side fall, even in a very large balance.

questions.question: What does the balance example help us understand about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It helps us understand that small causes and great results are equally easy under His laws and wisdom.

questions.question: What qualities of Allah’s power are connected to order and balance in creation?
questions.answer: His justice, wisdom, and perfect control.

questions.question: How does the passage compare moving stars and moving atoms?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: In spring, what two levels of giving life are mentioned to show Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Giving life to one fly and giving life to whole groups of plants and animals.

questions.question: How is bringing life back to a tree compared with reviving the earth in spring?
questions.answer: Both are described as easy for Allah.

questions.question: What does the earth in spring become like in this passage?
questions.answer: It becomes like something brought back to life after being dead.

questions.question: What is one strong proof in the passage that resurrection is possible?
questions.answer: Every spring, Allah brings life back to the earth and creates many living things again with ease.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of light is Allah’s pre-eternal power described as?
questions.answer: It is described as the finest and highest light.

questions.question: How are the inner realities of created things described?
questions.answer: They are described as shining like mirrors.

questions.question: What attitude do all things have toward Allah’s command?
questions.answer: They are fully obedient and under His control.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage make from this obedience?
questions.answer: Creating many things is just as easy as creating one thing.

questions.question: What does the passage say about different tasks for Allah?
questions.answer: One task never gets in the way of another.

questions.question: What pairs of opposites are said to be the same for Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Great and small, many and few, and individual and universal.

questions.question: What example is given from daily life about a child and a toy?
questions.answer: A child can push a toy easily, and this is used as an example of easy movement under order.

questions.question: Why is the ship example important?
questions.answer: It shows that something huge can be directed smoothly through law and order.

questions.question: What does the commander example teach about command?
questions.answer: A single command can guide either one soldier or a whole army.

questions.question: In the mountain-and-scale example, what is surprising?
questions.answer: A very small thing can affect a balance holding something as huge as mountains.

questions.question: What does this surprising example help the reader infer?
questions.answer: That size does not limit what can happen when wise laws are at work.

questions.question: Which two qualities are named as the source of order and regularity in creation?
questions.answer: Divine justice and endless wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage connect Allah’s wisdom to the life of flies in spring?
questions.answer: It says He gives life to one fly and to all flies with the same ease.

questions.question: Besides flies, what other living groups are mentioned as being brought to life in spring?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: How does the last sentence connect spring to resurrection?
questions.answer: It says spring shows many examples of coming back to life, which points to resurrection.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the relationship between number and difficulty for Allah?
questions.answer: Having more things does not make anything harder for Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe created things in relation to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It describes them as bright and ready to receive His command like mirrors.

questions.question: Which is easier for Allah according to the passage: creating one thing or many things?
questions.answer: Both are equally easy.

questions.question: What does the phrase about tasks not interfering with each other mean in simple words?
questions.answer: It means Allah can do many things at once without any problem.

questions.question: What is the point of mentioning atoms, plants, animals, stars, suns, and moons together?
questions.answer: It shows that all levels of creation are under the same divine command.

questions.question: What does the huge ship example show about order?
questions.answer: Order makes the movement of something very large happen in a controlled and easy way.

questions.question: What does the army example show about authority?
questions.answer: Real authority can direct one or many with the same command.

questions.question: Why does the passage use the picture of a balance with mountains?
questions.answer: To show that under a precise law, even a tiny addition can move something enormous.

questions.question: What can a student learn from these examples taken together?
questions.answer: Allah’s power works through perfect wisdom, law, and order, so size and number do not matter.

questions.question: What is said to be the beginning and foundation of order in creation?
questions.answer: Allah’s justice and wisdom within His eternal power.

questions.question: How are stars and atoms compared?
questions.answer: Both are moved by Allah with equal ease.

questions.question: What springtime example shows that whole groups can be revived together?
questions.answer: The whole kinds of flies, plants, and animals are given life.

questions.question: What happens to the earth in spring according to the final lines?
questions.answer: It is revived like a dead body coming back to life.

questions.question: What are the “many examples” of resurrection in spring?
questions.answer: The many different living things that return to life again.

questions.question: What overall belief does this passage strengthen?
questions.answer: It strengthens belief that Allah can resurrect all creation easily.

questions.question: What special quality of Allah’s power is emphasized at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It is pure, radiant, eternal, and above all limits.

questions.question: Why are created things compared to mirrors?
questions.answer: Because they receive and show the effects of Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the obedience of creation?
questions.answer: Every created thing follows Allah’s command completely.

questions.question: How does this obedience help explain creation?
questions.answer: It explains why many things can be created together with no difficulty.

questions.question: What statement in the passage shows Allah is never overwhelmed?
questions.answer: No task prevents another task for Him.

questions.question: Which example uses a child to explain an important idea?
questions.answer: The example of a child moving a toy.

questions.question: What idea does that child example help explain?
questions.answer: That something large can be moved easily under proper order.

questions.question: Which example compares one person with a large group?
questions.answer: The example of one soldier and a whole army.

questions.question: What does that example teach about one command?
questions.answer: The same command can direct both little and much.

questions.question: What natural rule is pictured by the balance example?
questions.answer: A balanced system responds in an exact way even to a small addition.

questions.question: How is that rule used to help explain Allah’s actions in creation?
questions.answer: It shows that through His wise laws, great things can be moved as easily as small things.

questions.question: Which two traits of Allah are directly tied to order and balance?
questions.answer: His justice and His wisdom.

questions.question: What comparison is made between one fly and all flies?
questions.answer: Giving life to one and to all is equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What larger event is compared to reviving a tree in spring?
questions.answer: Reviving the whole earth in spring.

questions.question: How does the passage use spring to teach about the Hereafter?
questions.answer: It presents spring as a clear sign that resurrection is easy for Allah.

questions.question: In this passage, what makes it reasonable that countless things can be created easily?
questions.answer: Allah’s eternal power, the readiness of creation, and the obedience of all things to His command.

questions.question: What does the passage say about placing many things side by side?
questions.answer: It says this is natural and easy for Allah.

questions.question: What do the words “particular” and “universal” point to here?
questions.answer: They point to single things and broad groups, which are both easy for Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both tiny and huge parts of creation?
questions.answer: To show that all sizes are equal before Allah’s power.

questions.question: What can we understand from the ship example besides simple movement?
questions.answer: We can understand that power works with order and control.

questions.question: In the commander example, what stays the same whether one soldier or many are sent?
questions.answer: The single command.

questions.question: What does that sameness teach us?
questions.answer: It teaches that number does not make command harder.

questions.question: What does the example of the walnut and the mountains show about balance?
questions.answer: A very small input can affect a very large system.

questions.question: Why is wisdom important in the balance example?
questions.answer: Because the result happens according to a measured and purposeful rule.

questions.question: What is said to be the source of order, regularity, and balance in creation?
questions.answer: Allah’s justice and endless wisdom within His power.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the response of all things to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: They obey it and submit to it.

questions.question: What examples from space and from tiny matter are used together?
questions.answer: Stars and atoms.

questions.question: What season is used as a living proof in this passage?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: How does spring show many forms of rising again?
questions.answer: Many plants and animals come to life, and the earth is revived after seeming dead.

questions.question: If a student had to give the best summary of the passage in one sentence, what could it be?
questions.answer: Allah’s wise and perfect power brings all things to life and controls all creation with complete ease.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give for Allah’s power at the beginning?
questions.answer: It presents Allah’s power as the highest and purest light.

questions.question: How are the realities inside created things described in relation to that power?
questions.answer: They are described as shining and able to reflect it like mirrors.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the behavior of all created things toward Allah’s orders?
questions.answer: They all submit and obey.

questions.question: Based on the passage, why is creating many things not a burden for Allah?
questions.answer: Because everything is under His command and His power has no difficulty.

questions.question: What truth is repeated through the phrases about great and small, many and few?
questions.answer: All of them are equal before Allah’s power.

questions.question: How does the ship example help a 5th-grade reader imagine this idea?
questions.answer: It shows that something huge can be moved simply and smoothly.

questions.question: How does the soldier-and-army example build on the same lesson?
questions.answer: It shows that one order can handle either one or many.

questions.question: In the scale example, why is the walnut important even though it is small?
questions.answer: It shows that a small thing can cause a big change in a balanced system.

questions.question: What do all three examples have in common?
questions.answer: They all teach that size and number do not make control difficult when there is perfect order.

questions.question: What are the roots of that perfect order according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are Allah’s justice and wisdom.

questions.question: What heavenly bodies are mentioned as being moved by Allah?
questions.answer: The stars.

questions.question: What tiny things are mentioned with them to make a comparison?
questions.answer: The atoms.

questions.question: What living example from spring is given first: one creature or a whole group?
questions.answer: First one fly is mentioned, then the whole species and many other living groups.

questions.question: What is compared to bringing a tree back to life in spring?
questions.answer: Bringing the earth back to life in spring.

questions.question: What belief about resurrection does this passage encourage Muslims to hold with confidence?
questions.answer: It encourages them to believe that Allah can raise all creation again easily and perfectly.
